description.narrative: Financing to Luminova Pharma Company (Luminova or the Company) to support the execution of its strategic plan including: (i) international expansion; and (ii) increased capacity and new products launch (the Project). Luminova is one of the largest pharma companies based in Central America engaged in the development, manufacture, and commercialization of generic pharmaceuticals. With two manufacturing facilities in Guatemala and more than 950 employees, Luminova has capacity for solids, semisolids, liquids, and injectables in the main therapeutical units including acute care (antibiotics, self-care, nutrition, anemia, respiratory self-care), and chronic care (cardio, diabetes, CNS, dyslipidemias, venous system, urology).

The Project responds to the growing need for affordable and high-quality pharmaceuticals in LAC . This region faces substantial challenges affording and accessing the pharmaceuticals, and the needs are particularly acute in IDA countries which are often relatively under-served due to the small market size and regulatory barriers to entry for new generics. The need for an appropriate range of affordable medication will be accentuated as these countries often face substantial increases in non-communicable diseases, the ongoing burden from communicable diseases and the potential for infectious disease outbreaks.
This project responds to this challenge by financing Luminovas strategic plan which includes expansion in a number of markets including in CA, which will be facilitated by the acquisition of a manufacturing facility located in Spain. This will expedite exports to LAC as it is easier to register products given EMA approval. The Company will implement a technology transfer from Guatemala to the company in Spain, obtain the registries there (EMA), for some of the products use the production facility in Spain to complete the last part of the production process (filling, packaging, etc.) and then export from there to LAC. In this way, the acquisition in Spain will facilitate an increase in production from Guatemala and the entry of the company into new developing markets.
The project will directly benefit patients through the increased production of medicines, and improved variety as new products are introduced to markets. This will strengthen their performance as Luminovas entry can be expected to increase levels of competition which will lead to lower prices and more variety.
